newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says importing $100 mln more sugar this year.
newsitem.headline: Iran says importing $100 mln more sugar this year.

text.p: Iran is importing $100 million more sugar this year due to a fall in domestic production, the Iranian industry minister said in remarks published on Sunday.

Mohammad Reza Nematzadeh, quoted by the daily Hamshahri, said the increasing imports in the Iranian year to March 20, 1998 resulted from falling sugar beet output as many farmers turned to more lucrative crops.
As part of a drive to fight spiralling prices, the government in the past two years put a ceiling on its purchase price for beet from local farmers, Nematzadeh said.
Subsequently, Tehran had decided to raise the price to lure farmers back to beet growing, he said.
The newspaper said the government had earlier set a price of 125,000 rials ($42) per tonne of beet for the current year, but it did not give the new, higher price.

Nematzadeh also blamed the low output on inefficient farming, saying Iranian farmers produced only up to 35 tonnes of beet per hectare while the world standard was as high as 55 tonnes per hectare, the newspaper added.
European sugar traders said last week Iran may have bought four cargoes of white sugar for shipment between May and July.
($1=3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
